mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which in turn predicts negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the predicted negative returns are not statistically distinguishable from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.0% for two consecutive months indicates an overheating labor market, which historically precedes either a slowdown in hiring or preemptive rate hikes, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is not robust in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly below zero during triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a demand-driven recovery.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (inflation) above their respective 12-month averages signals a stagflationary tightening, which compresses real cash flows and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during joint trigger episodes, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) above its 12-month maximum, combined with a concurrent decline in Real Personal Savings (RSAFS), signals a housing-driven demand surge with limited financing capacity, which historically precedes equity market corrections over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes, or the interaction is not robust across subperiods.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in PAYEMS above its long-run trend for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which in a late-cycle context predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to optimistic earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > long-run trend for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a subsequent recession.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in Real Personal Consumption Expenditures (GDPC1) combined with a concurrent rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over two quarters signals a deepening recession, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of monetary policy stance.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 declining AND UNRATE rising for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during joint trigger episodes, or the mechanism fails in non-recessionary periods.
